messages:
jess (support): Hey team, Acme Inc. reporting sudden p99 spike on hosted API since 09:22 UTC. Customer sees 3x tail latency and some 500s. Attaching a small log excerpt and their tenant id: tenant=acme-inc

oncall-bot: ALERT: tenant=acme-inc p99 latency 1.8s (>1.0s threshold). GPU memory usage on nodes serving tenant is at 98%, OOM kill events detected. Incident ticket: INC-4621 created.

omar (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the model name + typical seq length and concurrency? also any recent rollout for that tenant?

jess (support): model=redwood-realm-13b-quant, seq~2048 (mostly ~1.2k), peak concurrency reported ~28 simultaneous requests. No recent customer config changes on our side, but they did upload a big ingestion job ~1h before spike. Logs: 
```
2025-06-11T09:22:17Z ERROR: GPU OOM allocating 512MB for KV
2025-06-11T09:22:17Z WARN: slab_fragmentation_ratio=0.87 kv_growth_bytes=4.3GB
2025-06-11T09:22:18Z INFO: evict_attempts=5 evicted_bytes=120MB
```

liam (eng-sre): sounds like KV growth + fragmentation. Immediate ask: can we route this tenant to a smaller model variant while we triage? fallback to redwood-realm-7b-quant should reduce pressure. I can flip a route rule.

omar (eng-runtime): agree. Also quick mitigation: enable aggressive KV eviction and reduce per-tenant KV cache limit. We have admin flags: 
```
POST /admin/tenant/acme-inc/config \n{ "kv_cache_limit_mb": 512, "kv_eviction_policy": "aggressive", "kv_ttl_seconds": 300 }
```
That will force stale prefixes out faster. Recommend doing fallback routing + kv_ttl first.

tara (support-engineer): will fallback impact quality for the customer? they asked about SLA implications.

omar (eng-runtime): small model will increase generation latency slightly on median but should massively reduce tail blowups from OOM-related stalls. We should communicate a temporary quality degradation. For SLA, mark as mitigated if p99 < 1s after changes.

liam (eng-sre): operational steps I propose now:
1) apply tenant route to 7b (canary one region)
2) set kv_ttl=300 and kv_cache_limit_mb=512
3) on affected nodes, trigger allocator compaction pass (non-disruptive) and then rolling restart if compaction doesn't free enough contiguous memory.

omar (eng-runtime): compaction command (internal):
```
./runtimectl node compaction --node node-aws-gpu-12 --mode slab_compact
# if <free_contiguous_mb> < 1024 then schedule restart
```
Note: compaction can be noisy; do it on 2 nodes at a time.

jess (support): done the route and kv flag change in staging for a quick smoke. staging p99 dropped from 1.9s -> 0.45s. applying to prod now (will post logs).

oncall-bot: ACTION: applied route fallback -> redwood-realm-7b-quant for tenant=acme-inc. kv_ttl set to 300s. Monitoring p99.

omar (eng-runtime): for repro — to validate locally you can replay customer's pattern: 
```
replay-traffic --tenant acme-inc --rps 30 --pattern file://acme-pattern.json --duration 10m
```
That reproduces KV growth pattern we saw. Use that against a canary node and watch `kv_growth_bytes` and `slab_fragmentation_ratio`.

liam (eng-sre): long-term items I'll raise with infra: reduce default per-tenant kv_cache_limit and add an early warning metric: kv_growth_rate > 200MB/min -> autoscale or throttle. Also we should look at allocator settings; we saw fragmentation high when many 512B-4KB allocations persisted in KV. Candidate tuning: smaller slab classes, more frequent compaction, and reduce allocator cache windows.

omar (eng-runtime): one more immediate change we can toggle: enable \"evict-on-alloc-fail\" which will make runtime evict prefixes synchronously when allocation fails, avoiding retries that pile up and inflate p99. internal flag: `runtime.eviction.sync_on_alloc_fail=true`. Turning that on reduced p99 in our simulators.

jess (support): prod metrics after changes: p99 down to 0.62s at 09:30, errors 500 -> near zero. Customer says traffic resumed normal levels. I'll keep ticket updated and schedule follow-up call to explain fallback.

tara (support-engineer): please add notes to incident ticket with exact commands and timestamps so CS can share with Acme. I'll draft customer message.

liam (eng-sre): follow-up plan: 1) post-mortem to capture root cause = KV growth from ingestion + allocator fragmentation, 2) ship telemetry alert, 3) consider default limit changes and compaction cadence change, 4) longer-term allocator improvements.

omar (eng-runtime): agree. I'll also add a runtime patch to auto-detect sustained kv_growth and flip eviction.sync_on_alloc_fail for that tenant automatically.

oncall-bot: UPDATE: incident INC-4621 status=mitigated. p99 back under threshold. Owners: eng-runtime, eng-sre, support.

jess (support): closing loop with customer now, will reopen if anything else pops up. thanks all :thumbsup:
